title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 78 (Registration application by charge holder)

content.overview: If a company fails to register a charge within the section 77 period, the charge-holder may apply to the Registrar with the charge instrument. After notice to the company, the Registrar may allow registration unless the company registers the charge or shows sufficient cause. The charge-holder may recover the prescribed registration fees paid from the company.

content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 78 (Registration application by charge-holder). If the company fails to register a charge within the period specified in section 77, without prejudice to the company's liability under the chapter, the person in whose favour the charge was created may apply to the Registrar for registration with the instrument creating the charge, within the prescribed time and manner. The Registrar may, after giving notice to the company and unless the company itself registers the charge or shows sufficient cause to the contrary, allow registration on payment of prescribed fees. Where registration is effected on the charge-holder's application, the charge-holder is entitled to recover from the company the fees or additional fees paid to the Registrar. This is a fallback route; it does not remove the company's primary duty under section 77. Legal verification remains open.

misconceptions.trap: Treating section 78 as replacing the company's primary duty to register a charge.

misconceptions.trap: Assuming the Registrar must register the charge immediately on the charge-holder's application.
misconceptions.correction: The Registrar gives notice to the company and may allow registration unless the company registers or shows sufficient cause.

misconceptions.trap: Omitting the charge-holder's right to recover registration fees.
misconceptions.correction: Section 78 allows recovery from the company of the fees or additional fees paid where registration is effected on the charge-holder's application.
